title: Doanh nhân Phạm Nhật Vượng và những cuộc “bắt đầu lại” trên đỉnh cao
description: Từ bất động sản, du lịch đến ô tô, năng lượng và đường sắt, tỷ phú Phạm Nhật Vượng, Chủ tịch Tập đoàn Vingroup liên tục lựa chọn những lĩnh vực mới khi đang đứng trên đỉnh thành công. Đằng sau những cuộc “bắt đầu lại” ấy là khát vọng chứng minh năng lực của người Việt với thế giới.
content_md:
Từ bất động sản, du lịch đến ô tô, năng lượng và đường sắt, tỷ phú Phạm Nhật Vượng, Chủ tịch Tập đoàn Vingroup liên tục lựa chọn những lĩnh vực mới khi đang đứng trên đỉnh thành công. Đằng sau những cuộc “bắt đầu lại” ấy là khát vọng chứng minh năng lực của người Việt với thế giới.

Đầu những năm 2000, một đoàn doanh nhân và đối tác từ Nga, Ukraine sang Việt Nam với gần nửa máy bay chứa chứa đồ ăn. Họ vẫn hình dung Việt Nam là một đất nước nghèo khó, thiếu thốn sau chiến tranh. Nhưng khi đến khu nghỉ dưỡng Vinpearl vừa hoàn thành trên đảo Hòn Tre, Nha Trang – họ hoàn toàn bị bất ngờ trước sự hiện đai và thịnh vượng mà người Việt xây dựng. Đây là lời kể từ một người bạn của tỷ phú Phạm Nhật Vượng trên báo *Thanh Niên* năm 2019.

Hơn một thập kỷ sau, Vingroup tiếp tục "gây sửng sốt" với công bố sản xuất ô tô thương hiệu Việt, đồng thời ra mắt xe concept ngay trong năm sau – điều mà các hãng ô tô mạnh nhất thế giới cũng cần tối thiểu 3–4 năm chuẩn bị.

Hai câu chuyện cách nhau hơn thập kỷ rưỡi nhưng có một điểm chung. Từ du lịch nghỉ dưỡng đến sản xuất ô tô, ông Vượng đều lựa chọn những công việc mà năng lực của doanh nghiệp Việt Nam chưa được nhìn nhận đầy đủ, với mong muốn chứng minh người Việt có thể làm được những điều từng bị xem là quá sức.

Gần một thập kỷ sau công bố VinFast, tháng 10/2026, Vingroup tiếp tục ký thỏa thuận với Alstom, tập đoàn công nghệ đường sắt của Pháp, về 200 đoàn tàu metro phục vụ các dự án đường sắt đô thị Hà Nội. Trong đó, 83 đoàn dự kiến sản xuất tại Pháp, còn 117 đoàn được định hướng lắp ráp tại Việt Nam theo giấy phép công nghệ, với sự hỗ trợ kỹ thuật và linh kiện từ Alstom.

Thỏa thuận đánh dấu bước tham gia mới của Vingroup vào làn sóng đầu tư hạ tầng giao thông tại Việt Nam. Không chỉ đầu tư các tuyến đường sắt, tập đoàn còn muốn từng bước tham gia sản xuất phương tiện, một lĩnh vực mà doanh nghiệp trong nước chưa có nhiều kinh nghiệm.

Từ khu nghỉ dưỡng Hòn Tre đến nhà máy ô tô Hải Phòng và nay là công nghiệp đường sắt, ông Phạm Nhật Vượng liên tục đưa doanh nghiệp bước vào những lĩnh vực mới với khát vọng phụng sự và cống hiến ngày càng rõ nét. Phần lớn những quyết định ấy được đưa ra khi ông đã đạt được thành công đủ lớn để có thể lựa chọn một con đường kinh doanh an toàn hơn.

**Lựa chọn "bắt đầu lại" từ…. đỉnh**

Ông Phạm Nhật Vượng từng có ý định nghỉ kinh doanh từ rất sớm.

Trong cuộc phỏng vấn với *Forbes Việt Nam* năm 2013, ông kể rằng khi hoạt động sản xuất mì ăn liền ở Ukraine bắt đầu có lợi nhuận vào khoảng năm 1997–1998, ông từng nghĩ đến việc tích lũy khoảng 2 triệu USD rồi nghỉ làm, dành thời gian đi chơi.

Nhưng kế hoạch ấy không trở thành hiện thực. Ông Vượng rời hoạt động kinh doanh sản xuất thực phẩm đã xây dựng được vị thế lớn tại Ukraine, tập trung phát triển Vingroup ở Việt Nam. Từ Vinpearl, Vincom đến Vinhomes, tập đoàn tiếp tục tạo dựng những thương hiệu lớn trong bất động sản và dịch vụ.

Thành công của một dự án không đồng nghĩa Vingroup sẽ dừng lại hoặc chạy chậm đi. Năm 2013, Vingroup hoàn tất thương vụ chuyển nhượng Vincom Center A tại TP.HCM với giá hơn 9.823 tỷ đồng, tương đương khoảng 470 triệu USD. Đây là một tổ hợp thương mại, khách sạn cao cấp vừa đi vào hoạt động và từng được xem là công trình tiêu biểu của tập đoàn. Nhưng khi được hỏi vì sao bán một tài sản như vậy, ông Vượng giải thích rằng bất động sản nào được giá tốt thì có thể bán để lấy nguồn lực xây dựng những dự án khác.

Quan điểm ấy tiếp tục xuất hiện trong những quyết định sau này. Năm 2019, khi hệ thống VinMart, VinMart+ đã phát triển tới hàng nghìn điểm bán, Vingroup quyết định chuyển giao VinCommerce và VinEco cho Masan thông qua thương vụ hoán đổi cổ phần. Tại thời điểm công bố, Vingroup cho biết muốn tập trung nguồn lực cho lĩnh vực công nghiệp và công nghệ.

Đến năm 2024, tập đoàn tiếp tục chuyển nhượng toàn bộ vốn tại SDI, giảm lượng cổ phần nắm giữ tại Vincom Retail.

Các hoạt động chuyển giao và tái cơ cấu danh mục đầu tư được sử dụng để thu hồi vốn, điều chỉnh ưu tiên và tạo nguồn lực cho những kế hoạch tiếp theo. Trong số đó, VinFast là cuộc chuyển hướng từng gây sốc bởi đây là một lĩnh vực đòi hỏi nguồn vốn rất lớn, công nghệ phức tạp và thời gian tích lũy kinh nghiệm kéo dài.

Chỉ sau 9 tháng của năm 2026, VinFast đã bàn giao 177.697 xe ô tô điện, không chỉ duy trì vị trí dẫn đầu doanh số liên tục tại Việt Nam từ năm 2024 đến nay, mà còn thiết lập kỷ lục về doanh số chưa thương hiệu ô tô nào đạt được trên thị trường nội địa.

Tuy nhiên, để đạt được quy mô ấy, VinFast cần rất nhiều nguồn lực, đặc biệt là tài chính. Lúc này, ông Phạm Nhật Vượng – trên cương vị là người sáng lập, đã trở thành điểm tựa vững chắc. Phát biểu tại Đại hội đồng cổ đông Vingroup tháng 4/2024, ông tuyên bố "sẽ không bao giờ buông VinFast".

Theo báo cáo tài chính hợp nhất của Vingroup, trong 6 tháng đầu năm 2026, ông Phạm Nhật Vượng tiếp tục tài trợ thêm hơn 12.500 tỷ đồng cho công ty con của tập đoàn, được cho là dành cho VinFast. Tính từ năm 2024, tổng giá trị các khoản tài trợ được ghi nhận đạt gần 43.900 tỷ đồng. Đổi lại, VinFast liên tiếp giữ vững thị phần số 1 Việt Nam về ô tô điện kể từ tháng 10/2024.

**Những cuộc "bắt đầu mới" trong lĩnh vực nền tảng**

Nếu VinFast đánh dấu bước chuyển của ông Phạm Nhật Vượng từ bất động sản sang công nghiệp chế tạo, thì những quyết định gần đây cho thấy mục tiêu của ông còn đi xa hơn việc sản xuất ô tô. Năm 2024, ông thành lập V-Green để phát triển hạ tầng trạm sạc, đồng thời mở rộng hệ sinh thái giao thông xanh với Xanh SM và VinBus. Tháng 3/2026, V-Green công bố kế hoạch đầu tư 10.000 tỷ đồng xây dựng 99 siêu trạm sạc trên các trục giao thông lớn, mỗi trạm có thể phục vụ đồng thời tới 100 ô tô điện.

Không dừng ở đó, tháng 3/2025, ông Vượng tiếp tục bước vào lĩnh vực năng lượng với việc thành lập VinEnergo. Chỉ một năm sau, doanh nghiệp công bố các thỏa thuận triển khai danh mục dự án năng lượng tái tạo quốc tế có tổng quy mô 10 GW, hướng tới phát triển điện gió, điện mặt trời và công nghệ lưu trữ năng lượng.

Ở lĩnh vực luyện kim, tháng 2/2026, dự án nhà máy thép VinMetal tại Hà Tĩnh được cấp giấy chứng nhận đầu tư với tổng vốn gần 80.000 tỷ đồng, công suất thiết kế giai đoạn 1 là 6 triệu tấn mỗi năm, dự kiến nâng lên 20 triệu tấn mỗi năm trong giai đoạn 2. Nhà máy dự kiến sản xuất thép cán nóng, thép cường độ cao và thép hợp kim đặc chủng phục vụ ngành ô tô, công nghiệp và hạ tầng giao thông.

Đặc biệt, giữa lúc Việt Nam thúc đẩy đầu tư phát triển hạ tầng giao thông, ông Vượng tiếp tục đưa Vingroup vào lĩnh vực hạ tầng. Tập đoàn đã khởi công 2 tuyến đường sắt tốc độ cao là Bến Thành – Cần Giờ (TP HCM) và Hà Nội – Quảng Ninh, sử dụng đoàn tàu thế hệ mới Velaro Novo và công nghệ của Siemens Mobility (Đức).

Bên cạnh đó, tại 5 tuyến đường sắt đô thị Hà Nội mà liên danh Vinhomes – SGC là tổng thầu, Vingroup đã hợp tác với Alstom để cho ra số lượng 200 đoàn tàu metro, trong đó 117 đoàn dự kiến được lắp ráp tại Việt Nam theo giấy phép công nghệ, cho thấy doanh nghiệp không chỉ muốn đầu tư các tuyến đường sắt mà còn tham gia sản xuất phương tiện, từng bước tiếp cận công nghệ và phát triển đội ngũ kỹ thuật trong nước.

Từ ô tô điện đến năng lượng, luyện kim và hạ tầng, ông Phạm Nhật Vượng đang tiếp tục bước vào những lĩnh vực đầy thử thách, đòi hỏi vốn lớn, công nghệ phức tạp và thời gian đầu tư kéo dài. Nhưng chính việc liên tục lựa chọn những công việc khó, ngay cả khi đã đạt được thành công lớn trong những ngành kinh doanh khác, là một nét nổi bật trong hành trình dấn thân của vị tỷ phú này.

Sau hơn ba thập kỷ kinh doanh, với ông Phạm Nhật Vượng, thành công không phải lý do để dừng lại, mà trở thành nguồn lực để bắt đầu những khát vọng mới, với quy mô, mức độ thử thách cũng như tinh thần cống hiến ngày càng lớn. Đó cũng chính là điểm chung thường thấy ở những doanh nhân thành công trên thế giới.

title: Gold tumbles below $4,200 on higher oil prices, firmer US Dollar
content_md:
Gold price (XAU/USD) falls to around $4,170 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. The precious metal retreats from a one-week high on a stronger US Dollar (USD) and higher crude oil prices. Traders await the key US inflation data later this week for more clues on the Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest-rate trajectory.

Oil prices jump to a two-week high amid hopes of a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire and a new round of Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. These developments raise inflation concerns, prompting central bank tightening. Gold is often used as an inflation hedge but pays no interest, making it less attractive when interest rates are high.

“The macro backdrop remains challenging as persistent inflationary pressures continue to keep additional Fed tightening on the table, supporting Treasury yields and maintaining pressure on real rates,” said Manav Modi, a commodities analyst at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.

On the other hand, rising demand might help limit the yellow metal’s losses. Inflows into gold-backed ETFs have reached a four-year high, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Additionally, the Chinese central bank added 740,000 ounces to its reserves in September, extending its buying streak to 23 consecutive months.

#### Gold gains as CTAs cover shorts and TD Securities eyes bull run into 2027

According to strategists at TD Securities, commodity trading advisors are now “covering shorts across gold and platinum as strong fundamental backdrop for precious metals insulates the market.” The bank notes that “the yellow metal is gaining on the day with CTAs back on the bid, covering shorts by some 7% of historic max position size,” underscoring a meaningful shift in positioning. TD Securities argues that “geopolitical risk, fiscal concern, dollar debasement, de-dollarization and stagflation concerns all remain major supportive factors for these flows in gold,” and concludes that “we continue to see the stage being set for the yellow metal to disconnect from real rates further and begin a new bull run into 2027.”

#### Technical Analysis: Gold retains a negative tone below the 100-day SMA

In the daily chart, XAU/USD keeps a bearish near-term tone as spot holds beneath the 20-day Bollinger middle band and the 100-day simple moving average (SMA). This alignment leaves gold locked below its primary trend gauges, while the Relative Strength Index (RSI) at 43.73 leans lower, suggesting downside pressure persists but without oversold conditions.

On the topside, initial resistance is located at the Bollinger middle band near $4,225, followed by the 100-day SMA at $4,255; a daily close above these barriers would be needed to ease the current downside bias, with the upper Bollinger band at $4,400 acting as a more distant cap. On the downside, the lower Bollinger band at $4,055 offers the next notable support, and a break below that zone would open the door to a deeper corrective phase.

*(The technical analysis of this story was written with the help of an AI tool. Know more.)*

#### Gold FAQs

Gold has played a key role in human’s history as it has been widely used as a store of value and medium of exchange. Currently, apart from its shine and usage for jewelry, the precious metal is widely seen as a safe-haven asset, meaning that it is considered a good investment during turbulent times. Gold is also widely seen as a hedge against inflation and against depreciating currencies as it doesn’t rely on any specific issuer or government.

Central banks are the biggest Gold holders. In their aim to support their currencies in turbulent times, central banks tend to diversify their reserves and buy Gold to improve the perceived strength of the economy and the currency. High Gold reserves can be a source of trust for a country’s solvency. Central banks added 1,136 tonnes of Gold worth around $70 billion to their reserves in 2022, according to data from the World Gold Council. This is the highest yearly purchase since records began. Central banks from emerging economies such as China, India and Turkey are quickly increasing their Gold reserves.

Gold has an inverse correlation with the US Dollar and US Treasuries, which are both major reserve and safe-haven assets. When the Dollar depreciates, Gold tends to rise, enabling investors and central banks to diversify their assets in turbulent times. Gold is also inversely correlated with risk assets. A rally in the stock market tends to weaken Gold price, while sell-offs in riskier markets tend to favor the precious metal.

The price can move due to a wide range of factors. Geopolitical instability or fears of a deep recession can quickly make Gold price escalate due to its safe-haven status. As a yield-less asset, Gold tends to rise with lower interest rates, while higher cost of money usually weighs down on the yellow metal. Still, most moves depend on how the US Dollar (USD) behaves as the asset is priced in dollars (XAU/USD). A strong Dollar tends to keep the price of Gold controlled, whereas a weaker Dollar is likely to push Gold prices up.

content_md:
Australian shares are poised to rise on Tuesday, tracking higher oil prices as escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia fueled concerns over crude supply disruptions, while expectations of increased Russian diesel supplies and a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire on energy infrastructure offered some relief to global markets.

Overnight, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.1% and 0.4% respectively, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.4%.

In the macroeconomy, the ANZ-Roy Morgan Australian consumer confidence rose 0.9 points to 68 in the week of Oct. 5 to 11, ANZ reported Tuesday.

In corporate news, Arena REIT (ASX:ARF) said Edge Early Learning's administrator has entered into binding agreements or term sheets with six parties to sell 22 additional centers, including the remaining seven Edge-operated centers at Arena-owned properties.

Wildcat Resources (ASX:WC8) reported a cash balance of AU$76.1 million at the end of the September quarter, up from AU$37.2 million held at the bank as of June 30.

Australia's benchmark index rose 0.8%, or 66.6 points, to close at 8,783.20 on Monday.

The Dollar Index is hovering at **102.245**, nervously close to a potential double top just under its 102.305 peak. Market structure still favors bulls—price is firmly above the 200-period SMA (100.019) and well supported by the Ichimoku cloud and SuperTrend signal. However, the consolidation zone (101.75–102.20) and fading momentum (MACD bearish cross, RSI at 62.44) mean buyers look winded at these levels.

title: US Equity Markets Mixed Amid Rising Crude Oil Prices
content_md:
US equity indexes were mixed Monday as technology and consumer discretionary sectors fell and crude oil jumped amid reports of strikes between Russia and Ukraine.

\* All 20 worst performers were technology names among stocks with market capitalization exceeding $200 billion, according to data compiled by Finviz.

\* Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia targeted six energy facilities in Ukraine, BBC reported. Meanwhile, the Trump administration has warned Ukraine and allies in Europe that the US could suspend intelligence sharing and European purchases of US weapons for Ukraine if Kyiv does not halt its deep strikes on Russian energy facilities, two European officials told CNN.

\* November West Texas Intermediate crude oil rose $1.46 to settle at $93.31 per barrel, while December Brent crude, the global benchmark, was last seen up $1.46 at $106.18.

\* Meta Platforms (META) shares were up about 3.4%, among the best performers on the Nasdaq and S&P 500, after the company launched two frontier artificial intelligence models.

\* Ciena's (CIEN) shares fell nearly 10%, the worst performer on the S&P 500, after the company announced Monika Fahlbusch's appointment as its chief people officer, effective Monday.

#### Dollar Index tests 102.40 breakout as volume fades: Live levels

Published 12-10-2026, 07:39 pm

Updated 13-10-2026, 12:40 am

Dollar Index tests 102.40 breakout as volume fades: Live levels

© Reuters.

In this article:

**Latest update:** Oct 12, 2026, 07:09 PM UTC

This article is regularly updated during market hours

The Dollar Index just closed a 5-hour bar at **102.388**, with strong bullish structure—but signs of fatigue are emerging as volume drops and price hugs recent highs. The next move hinges on holding above **101.75** or breaking out past **102.40**; the battle between momentum and exhaustion is heating up.

#### Trend Still Hot—but Vulnerable

The Dollar Index is in a powerful, multi-session uptrend: price sits above key long-term (SMA 200 at 100.035) and short-term supports (SuperTrend at 101.844, Ichimoku Cloud’s upper edge at 102.008). But here’s where it gets interesting— **RSI at 65.98** flirts with overbought, and the latest surge to **102.388** came on shrinking volume (920 vs 722). That’s the classic sign of buyers tiring out just as resistance tightens.

#### Bullish Scenario: Breakout or Dip Buy?

**Two ways for bulls to play it:**

- **Aggressive:** If price closes above **102.40** (clear resistance and ascending channel cap), expect momentum to accelerate. Target levels: **102.65**, **103.00**, and a possible trend extension to **103.46** (127.2% Fibonacci).
- **Conservative:** If a pullback forms, the sweet spot is a bounce off **102.05** (near the 20-period average and inside the trend zone). Risk is carefully managed below **101.75**.

**What could go wrong?** A rally that fails here amid thinning volume could turn into a classic "bull trap." Keeping stops diligently below key support is vital.

#### Bearish Scenario: Fading the Euphoria

For counter-trend traders, patience and precision are essential:

- **Aggressive entry:** Wait for a bearish reversal pattern at **102.35**
- **Conservative:** Enter only after a breakdown with a 5-hour close below **101.70** (under SuperTrend support)
- **Stops:** Placed above **102.05**
- **Target zones:** **101.00**, **100.43**, and major support at **100.03**

**Warning:** The broader uptrend means this is a lower-confidence, higher-risk play unless sellers prove themselves with a breakdown.

#### Trade Scenarios at a Glance

|  | Bullish | Bearish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry Level | 102.45 (breakout) / 102.05 (pullback) | 102.35 (reversal) / 101.70 (breakdown) |
| Stop | 101.75 | 102.05 |
| Target 1 | 102.65 | 101.00 |
| Target 2 | 103.00 | 100.03 |
| Risk:Reward | 2.0–4.7 | 2.0–4.7 |
| Confidence | Medium | Low |
| Best For | Trend followers | Fast movers |

#### What to Watch Next

- **Support:** 101.75 (structural) and 102.05 (trend/pullback zone)
- **Resistance:** 102.40 (breakout trigger)
- **Volume:** Needs to expand to sustain any breakout—shrinking volume at these highs spells danger.
- **RSI:** Move above 70 warns of more exhaustion; reversal below 50 signals sellers are back.

#### Key Lesson: Don’t Chase Exhaustion

When price is trending but volume fades and momentum signals near exhaustion (like an RSI closing in on 70 and full Bollinger Band extension), the risk of a snapback grows fast. Let price prove its strength—chasing late in the move often means paying top rupee right before a turn.

title: US Dollar Strength Masks Growing Disconnect With Treasury Yields
content_md:
Advertisement

By David Scutt

Published10/12/2026, 02:38 AM

US Dollar Strength Masks Growing Disconnect With Treasury Yields

Articles(647) \| My Homepage

Follow

In this article:

US yields are falling, Fed tightening expectations are easing, yet the dollar remains firm. French debt concerns may help explain why, with several major currency pairs approaching important technical levels.

- DXY’s relationship with front-end yields abruptly turns negative
- Euro weakness offsets retreat in Fed tightening expectations
- US CPI backtesting reveals no consistent directional trading advantage
- DXY, EUR/USD and USD/JPY test important technical levels

#### **US Dollar Resilience Faces a Busy Week**

The US dollar enters a busy week for economic data, headlined by CPI, PPI and retail sales on Wednesday and Thursday. However, while those releases will be the headline acts, what may be of greater interest is the abrupt breakdown in the dollar’s relationship with front-end US Treasury yields.

Having maintained a generally positive relationship through much of this year, correlations have deteriorated sharply in October, with the dollar continuing to strengthen despite a partial reversal of September’s surge in US yields and reduced expectations for further Fed tightening. Without renewed concerns over France’s public finances weighing heavily on the euro, it’s possible the dollar would already be trading considerably lower.

#### **DXY’s Relationship with US Treasury Yields Breaks Down**

You can see the deterioration in the dollar’s relationship with front-end US Treasury yields in the graphic below. As recently as the end of September, the 10-session rolling correlation between DXY and US 2-year yields stood at +0.66, with the 20-session measure at +0.55. By the end of last week, those readings had fallen to −0.39 and +0.19, respectively.

_Source: LSEG_

Similar movements have been seen against 5-year yields in the belly of the curve, suggesting the change isn’t confined to just the front end. Since the end of September, DXY has risen around 0.75%, despite US 2-year yields falling 9.6 basis points and five-year yields declining 6.8 basis points over the same period.

#### **Fed Pricing Retreats, but the Dollar Holds Firm**

Following the softer US payrolls report earlier this month, along with what appears to have been a concerted effort by Fed officials to push back against expectations for another rate hike in October, markets have reduced their expectations for further tightening. As shown in the graphic below, cumulative tightening priced through the end of next year has fallen from just over 100 basis points in mid-September to around 80 basis points.

_Source: TradingView_

Had the dollar maintained the positive relationship with front-end Treasury yields seen earlier this year, it suggests that, all else being equal, the greenback would be weaker than where it is today.

However, currencies don’t trade on US developments alone. Renewed concerns over France’s public finances, fears of spillovers into other European debt markets and higher energy prices have weighed heavily on the euro. Given its 57.6% weighting in DXY, that weakness may explain why the dollar has remained so resilient despite the retreat in US rate expectations.

#### **CPI Brings Volatility, but Little Directional Certainty**

While there’s plenty of important US economic data coming our way this week, historical patterns offer little guidance on directional risks for the dollar. Backtesting of 188 CPI releases since 2011 shows that although the dollar tends to experience larger moves on inflation reporting days, there’s little evidence of a consistent tendency to either extend or reverse its prevailing trend.

That suggests traders should keep a close eye not only on the incoming US data, but also on developments in European debt markets, which may prove just as influential in determining where the dollar heads next.

#### **DXY: Bullish Continuation Pattern Takes Shape**

DXY is consolidating the strong bullish move that began in early September, coinciding with a sharp increase in market expectations for further Fed tightening.

Whether you call it a symmetrical triangle or a bull pennant, the price has now tested both sides of the structure on several occasions, with the trading range continuing to narrow as bullish momentum cools. RSI (14) has been setting lower highs and has returned towards the neutral 50 level, while MACD remains below its signal line, albeit still in positive territory.

Given the preceding rally, the formation suggests we may see an eventual bullish breakout take place, although confirmation is required via a break above the upper boundary of the structure.

The upper boundary of the structure currently sits just below 102.50, with rising trend support located just beneath 102.00. Beyond those levels, 102.535, the high set earlier this month, is the immediate upside level to watch.

A sustained break above 102.535 would strengthen the bullish continuation argument, potentially opening the door to 103.35, which acted as both support and resistance in late 2024 and early 2025. Beyond that, 104.68, the March 2025 swing high, is the next topside level of note.

On the downside, 101.80, the June 24 swing high, has attracted buying on the last two tests from below. Beneath that, 101.60 is another important level, having acted as resistance earlier this year. A break below the latter would put 101.026, the swing low set in late September, in play.

#### **EUR/USD: Downside Risks Persist Despite Fading Momentum**

Unsurprisingly, a similar pattern is developing in EUR/USD on the four-hourly timeframe, albeit in the opposite direction. Following the sharp decline since September, the price has been consolidating within a contracting range that resembles either a bear pennant or a symmetrical triangle.

Since bottoming at 1.1162 earlier this month, the price has continued to contract, even as momentum indicators show signs of improvement despite unresolved concerns in French debt markets. RSI (14) has been setting higher lows and has returned to the neutral 50 level, while MACD has crossed above its signal line and is trending higher, albeit remaining marginally in negative territory.

It’s a bearish continuation pattern, pointing to the risk of an eventual breakdown, although confirmation is still required.

On the downside, the lower boundary of the structure currently sits around 1.1165, just above the October swing low at 1.1162, making this an important support zone to watch. A breakdown would put 1.1065 in play, the swing low set in May 2025, with little other obvious technical support in between.

Overhead, 1.12429, the high set on Friday, is the immediate level to watch, followed by the upper boundary of the structure around 1.1260. Above that, 1.12855, where the formation began, is the next upside level of note. A break higher would put 1.1312 in play, the late-September low that subsequently gave way during the decline into October.

#### **USD/JPY: Higher Lows Put Resistance Under Pressure**

USD/JPY has repeatedly struggled to overcome resistance at 158.45 since early October, including another failed attempt earlier today. However, since bottoming at 156.40 in late September, we’ve seen a series of higher lows, with buyers stepping in at progressively shallower levels.

It’s not quite an ascending triangle, but it has that feel to it, with the price gradually squeezing higher towards horizontal resistance at 158.45. That makes 158.45 the immediate level to watch, with a break above potentially opening the door to 159.00 and 159.50.

On the downside, dips towards 157.50 and below have been bought over the past week, making that the first level to watch, followed by 157.00 and 156.40.

title: European Stocks Close Higher in Monday Trading; Crude Oil Prices Continue to Rise After Attacks on Saudi Arabia
content_md:
European stock markets closed higher in Monday trading as crude oil prices continued to rise following attacks on Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi forces over the weekend.

The Stoxx Europe rose 0.5%, Germany's DAX gained 0.7%, the FTSE 100 advanced 0.8%, France's CAC increased 0.2%, and the Swiss Market Index ended the session up 0.6%.

In corporate news, Deutsche Bank is in discussions with Malaysia's state fund 1Malaysia Development Bhd., or 1MDB, over a proposed settlement of a $1.1 billion lawsuit, Bloomberg reported Monday.

1MDB lawyer Lim Chee Wee told Malaysia's High Court that the fund had a settlement proposal during a separate hearing on Monday, Bloomberg reported. A hearing in the Deutsche Bank case is scheduled for Oct. 26.

1MDB, embroiled in a fraud scandal, still faces 51.4 billion ringgit ($12.6 billion) in financial obligations linked to the scandal, Bloomberg added, citing the government. Recovery efforts have so far generated 31.3 billion ringgit, Bloomberg reported, citing the government.

Deutsche Bank and 1MDB did not immediately respond to MT Newswires' request for comment.

Shares of Deutsche Bank increased 1.2% in Frankfurt.

ASML will increase prices by 10% for replacement parts used in its extreme ultraviolet and deep ultraviolet lithography systems supplied to South Korea, starting in January 2027, The Elec reported Sunday, citing industry sources.

Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix accepted the increase, which covers consumables and major replacement components, following discussions with ASML, according to the report.

ASML is also discussing equipment price increases with major customers, the report added.

ASML, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix did not immediately respond to MT Newswires' request for comment.

Shares of the Dutch semiconductor company lost 1.6% in Amsterdam.

Vodafone and KKR, along with other Oak Holdings 1 investors, are securing financing for a potential buyout of minority shareholders in Inwit, Reuters reported Sunday, citing two people familiar with the matter.

Oak Holdings 1 and French private equity firm Ardian, which own 39% and 32% of Inwit, respectively, are discussing financing with banks, while Abu Dhabi's Mubadala is expected to take a stake in the company as part of the plan, according to the report.

The potential deal comes amid a contract dispute with Inwit's main customers, Telecom Italia and Swisscom's Fastweb, which are seeking to renegotiate terms, Reuters added.

In a statement emailed to MT Newswires, Inwit said it had no information on the reported potential transaction and was unable to comment. KKR declined to comment, while Vodafone said it was not commenting on the story.

Ardian, GIP, and Mubadala did not immediately respond to MT Newswires' request for comment.

Shares of the British telecommunications operator fell 1.5% in London.

HSBC will start phasing out fixed-pay allowance payouts for senior staff at the start of 2027, in favor of bonuses, Bloomberg reported Monday, citing a company memo.

The move is in line with the ongoing overhaul led by HSBC Chief Executive Georges Elhedery, according to the report.

HSBC did not immediately respond to MT Newswires' request for a comment.

Shares of HSBC advanced 1.9% in London.

Stellantis Chief Executive Antonio Filosa said the notion of separating the company's European and US brands is "not plausible at all," Bloomberg reported Monday, citing an interview with the CEO.

The automaker also presented six concept cars ahead of the Paris Motor Show, among more than 60 vehicles the automotive giant exhibited at the weeklong event, the company said Sunday.

The cars included the hybrid-powered Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso, the fully electric 15,000-euro ($16,806) Citroen 2 CV, the DS F3VER, the Fiat Multiplay SUV, several Opel models, and the Peugeot RCZVision using new steer-by-wire technology, the company said.

Shares of Stellantis declined 1.3% in Paris.

TotalEnergies awarded Vallourec a contract to supply more than 16,000 metric tons of tubular products for Azerbaijan's Absheron gas field, the latter said Monday.

The deal includes premium oil country tubular goods and about 159 kilometers of corrosion-resistant line pipe for onshore and offshore applications, it said, adding that the Caspian Sea project aims to produce up to 6 billion cubic meters of gas annually and 47,000 barrels of condensate per day.

Shares of the French oil and gas major closed 0.6% higher in Paris.

Eni said Monday it had signed two binding agreements to sell 10% interests in selected upstream gas assets in Indonesia to Pertamina and Medco, citing value gains from exploration and development activities in the Kutei Basin.

Under the first agreement, Eni will sell its 10% interest in the East Sepinggan, North Ganal, and Rapak production sharing contracts to Pertamina, Indonesia's national energy company. Under the second agreement, Eni will sell its 10% interest in the West Ganal, East Ganal, Ganal and Muara Bakau production sharing contracts to Medco, a Southeast Asian energy company, Eni said.

The company did not disclose financial terms for either transaction, which remain subject to customary governmental and regulatory approvals.

Shares of the Italian oil and gas company was up 0.9% in Milan.

title: Oil Prices Rise as Russia Reportedly Hits Ukrainian Energy Infrastructure
content_md:
Oil prices were advancing Monday following reports of Russian strikes targeting energy facilities in Ukraine, despite President Donald Trump announcing an energy ceasefire between the countries last week.

Brent crude oil was up 2% to $106.81 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate gained 1.9% to $93.61. The two benchmarks are up again so far in October following three consecutive monthly gains.

In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump announced Russia and Ukraine agreed to an energy ceasefire, with immediate effect.

"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine," Trump wrote. "Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!"

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of violating the ceasefire and said it targeted six energy facilities in Ukraine, according to a BBC report.

Zelenskyy thanked the European Union for adopting new sanctions against Russia, the report added. "More pressure on Russian entities" is "the right and indispensable signal if we are serious about ending Russia's war," he reportedly said.

"We have supposedly had an energy ceasefire before, which did not result in a change," ING Bank analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey said in a note Monday. "This ceasefire still needs to be confirmed by Ukraine and Russia, and if it is, then the question becomes how sustainable it is."

Last week, Trump said on social media that Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to supply diesel to the US and global markets. The deal covers export of 300,000 metric tonnes of Russian diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 metric tonnes in November and 1 million metric tonnes in December.

"This will also see the US temporarily easing sanctions on Russian diesel," Patterson and Manthey wrote. "However, these initial volumes are still some distance away from the roughly (3 million metric tonnes) per month that Russia shipped in 2025, according to (London Stock Exchange Group) data."

On Sunday, one person was killed, and nearly a dozen were injured after Riyadh's international airport was struck for the second time by Yemen's Houthis in as many days, according to media reports. An earlier strike on King Khalid International Airport on Saturday killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

Saxo Bank, noting that oil prices initially eased after spiking on news of the Saudi airport attacks, said Monday that "resilient Middle East crude flows, Russia's partial lifting of its diesel export ban and President Trump's surprise decision to allow imports of Russian diesel, alongside claims that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to a so-called energy ceasefire, have helped offset renewed regional tensions."

title: Chinese Yuan: Trade détente and PBoC fix support Yuan – Commerzbank
content_md:
Commerzbank analysts highlight that Beijing’s new trade agreement with Brussels, alongside a US–China tariff framework, modestly improves China’s external backdrop. They note the PBoC’s USD/CNY fixing model points to a slightly stronger Yuan and that both USD-CNY and USD-CNH fell to 6.69 last week, as easing trade tensions reduce headwinds for China’s export sector and current account.

#### Sino‑EU deal and tariffs ease headwinds

"The trade detente, if formalised at the EU leaders' summit this week, would reduce one of the more significant external headwinds facing China's export-oriented manufacturing sector."

"Combined with the previously reported US-China agreement on a 30-for-30tariff reduction framework, the diplomatic backdrop is incrementally more supportive for Chinese trade flows heading into year-end."

"Markets will watch closely whether the EU safeguard mechanism, which reportedly remains the preferred enforcement tool, is structured in a way that preserves Chinese market access or functions as a de facto import cap."

"The outcome will have direct implications for China's current account trajectory and, by extension, the PBoC's tolerance for yuan appreciation."

"In FX, both USD-CNY and offshore USD-CNH fell 110 pips to 6.69 and fell 130 pips last week."

title: Gold prices struggle to hold early gains as U.S. dollar nears 18-month high, bond yields remain elevated - Kitco AM Report
content_md:
(Kitco NewsWire) – The gold market is struggling to maintain its recent recovery as persistent inflation pressures, elevated bond yields and a U.S. dollar trading near an 18-month high continue to create significant headwinds for the precious metal ahead of another critical week of economic data.

Gold prices started the week with modest gains, briefly trading above $4,200 an ounce during the Asian session; however, bullish momentum has faded as investors remain reluctant to take significant positions ahead of Wednesday's U.S. Consumer Price Index report.

Spot gold was last quoted around $4,156.20 an ounce ahead of the North American trading session, down nearly 1% on the day. The precious metal has been unable to build on last week's recovery after prices briefly fell below $4,100 an ounce. Despite the recent buying momentum, gold remains well below its August highs as investors continue to assess the implications of tighter monetary policy and stubborn inflation.

Silver is also struggling to maintain its recovery, with prices trading around $60.35 an ounce after briefly pushing above $61 earlier in the session.

The latest U.S. economic data continues to paint a complicated picture for financial markets as weakening consumer confidence contrasts with persistently elevated inflation expectations.

On Friday, the University of Michigan reported that its preliminary consumer sentiment index fell to 46.3 in October, down from 48.1 in September and below expectations of 47.6. The current economic conditions index dropped sharply to 44.7, its lowest reading on record.

At the same time, consumers' one-year inflation expectations increased to 4.7%, up from 4.6%, while longer-term expectations rose to 3.5% from 3.4%.

The disappointing sentiment data follows September's weaker-than-expected employment report, which showed that the U.S. economy created only 29,000 jobs, while the unemployment rate increased to 4.2%. Although signs of slowing economic growth would normally support expectations for looser monetary policy, persistent inflation pressures continue to complicate the Federal Reserve's outlook.

Market positioning remains tilted toward further monetary tightening, with interest rate futures reflecting roughly an 85% probability of at least one additional rate hike by December. Investors see only about a 17% chance of a rate increase at the October meeting. The divergence between slowing employment growth and elevated inflation expectations is keeping Treasury yields and the U.S. dollar supported, limiting gold's ability to sustain its recent recovery.

The U.S. dollar remains a significant obstacle for the precious metal, with the U.S. Dollar Index holding near 102.20, close to its highest level in approximately 18 months. (Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.)

Simon-Peter Massabni, Head of Business Development at XS.com, said that the dollar continues to benefit from the combination of persistent energy inflation, geopolitical uncertainty and elevated U.S. Treasury yields.

Massabni added that persistent inflation pressures are preventing central banks from easing monetary policy and forcing fixed-income markets to adjust to expectations for higher interest rates.

Although the dollar's strength is weighing on gold, analysts note that the precious metal continues to attract safe-haven interest as investors navigate deteriorating economic conditions and growing geopolitical uncertainty.

The ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran remains a significant source of uncertainty, particularly as negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have failed to produce a lasting resolution. Iranian officials have rejected U.S. proposals as inadequate, while renewed attacks on Saudi Arabian infrastructure and continued military deployments have raised concerns about further regional escalation. Although oil prices have eased following President Donald Trump's announcement of a proposed energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, the risk of renewed disruptions to Middle Eastern energy supplies remains elevated. Brent crude has retreated toward $105 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate is trading above $92 a barrel. For gold, the conflict remains a double-edged sword: geopolitical uncertainty supports safe-haven demand, but higher energy prices threaten to keep inflation elevated, reinforcing expectations for tighter monetary policy.

Meanwhile, the U.S. bond market continues to present another significant challenge for gold as the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield remains well above 5%, near levels not seen in almost two decades. Although rising yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets such as gold, analysts note that the reasons behind the bond market's weakness are becoming increasingly important. With U.S. sovereign debt exceeding $40 trillion and annual interest costs surpassing $1 trillion, investors are demanding greater compensation for the risks associated with holding long-term government debt. Persistent inflation, growing borrowing requirements and concerns about the sustainability of U.S. fiscal policy are contributing to higher term premiums. While these developments create immediate headwinds for gold, they could also reinforce its longer-term appeal as an alternative monetary asset and portfolio diversification tool.

Massabni said that despite the current headwinds, gold is approaching an important technical and fundamental turning point.

"The key question is not simply whether gold can rebound from this area, but whether the underlying economic and fundamental conditions are strong enough to turn a potential recovery into a more sustainable bullish trend," he said.

He identified the area between $4,155 and $4,177 an ounce as an important support zone, adding that a sustained recovery will depend on whether inflation data allows Treasury yields and the U.S. dollar to lose momentum.

However, he warned that stronger-than-expected inflation could reinforce expectations for additional monetary tightening, potentially exposing gold to renewed selling pressure.

The market's next major test will come Wednesday with the release of September's Consumer Price Index. Investors will be watching whether rising energy prices are becoming embedded in broader inflation pressures, particularly core consumer prices.

A softer-than-expected inflation report could ease expectations for further Federal Reserve rate hikes, providing some relief for gold and silver. Conversely, another upside inflation surprise could push bond yields and the dollar higher, increasing the risk of renewed selling pressure across the precious metals complex.

Gold's near-term outlook remains bearish as prices continue to trade below a descending trendline and longer-term moving averages. Initial support is seen at $4,175.03 an ounce, followed by $4,141.86 and $4,103.24. A break below these levels could expose further downside toward $4,067.42. On the upside, initial resistance is seen at $4,226.82, with a sustained break above that level potentially opening the door to $4,271.57 and $4,311.17. Analysts note that gold will need to overcome its declining trendline to establish a more sustainable bullish recovery.

title: European Stocks Rise as Oil Prices Ease and Investors Await US Inflation Data: DAX, CAC, FTSE100
content_md:
European stock markets traded mostly higher on Monday, extending their recovery from four-month lows reached in the previous session, as declining oil prices and easing geopolitical concerns supported investor sentiment.

The rebound followed comments from US President Donald Trump dismissing speculation about potential military action against Iran ahead of the US midterm elections, helping to ease concerns about a further escalation of tensions in the Middle East.

Expectations of a possible energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine also contributed to lower crude oil prices, providing some relief to European markets amid continued uncertainty over global energy supplies.

Eurozone government bond yields declined alongside oil prices after Trump announced an agreement to obtain diesel from Russia as part of efforts to reduce fuel costs.

The US president also blamed Ukraine for the conflict and the resulting energy crisis, marking a significant shift in his administration's public position ahead of the midterm elections.

Investors were also preparing for a series of important US economic releases and corporate earnings announcements later in the week.

Particular attention will be directed towards US consumer and producer price inflation figures, which could influence expectations for Federal Reserve monetary policy and the outlook for interest rates.

Among the major European benchmarks, Germany's DAX Index and the UK's FTSE 100 Index both advanced 0.9%, while France's CAC 40 Index gained 0.5%.

Banking stocks were among the stronger performers, with Commerzbank (TG:CBK), Deutsche Bank (TG:DBK), BNP Paribas (EU:BNP) and Lloyds Banking Group (LSE:LLOY) recording gains of between 1% and 2%.

The advances contributed to broader market strength as investors reassessed the outlook for economic growth, borrowing costs and corporate earnings.

In Germany, wind turbine manufacturer Nordex Group (TG:NDX1) recorded a sharp increase in its share price after reporting a 29.5% rise in third-quarter orders.

The improvement in order intake provided a positive indication of demand for the company's wind energy equipment, supporting investor interest in the renewable energy manufacturer.

Automotive group Stellantis (BIT:STLAM) also posted substantial gains after announcing a strategic shift towards more affordable electric vehicles at the Paris Motor Show.

The announcement highlighted the company's efforts to address vehicle affordability and changing consumer demand as competition intensifies across the electric vehicle market.

Gold (GC=F) December futures opened at **$4,220.80** per troy ounce on **Monday, October 12, 2026**, up 2.3% from Friday's closing price. Gold is moving back some this morning to **$4,204.20** per troy ounce as of 6:45 a.m. ET.

Gold prices opened in the $4,200 range this morning, something we didn't observe last week, but prices appear to be sliding back some in early trading.

With no economic data slated for release today, investors are weighing earnings reports set to be released later this week, with some of the nation's largest banks first in line to report. In addition, the AI bubble continues to grow, and inflation remains top of mind as Middle East conflict over the weekend has Brent crude (BZ=F) prices above $105 a barrel this morning.

Expectations for future rate increases remain about the same as last week, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool, so gold prices continue to hang in a range that is more wait-and-see than strongly trending in one direction or another.

#### Current price of gold

Gold futures opened up 2.3% on **Monday, October 12, 2026**, from Friday's close. Here's a look at how the opening gold price has changed versus last week, month, and year:

- One week ago: +1.2%

*Want to learn more about the current top-performing companies in the gold industry?* Explore a list of the top-performing companies in the gold industry using the Yahoo Finance Screener. You can create your own screeners with over 150 different screening criteria.

#### Gold prices explained

The price of gold can be quoted in multiple forms because the precious metal is traded in different ways. The two main gold prices investors should know about are spot prices and gold futures prices.

*Learn more: How to invest in gold in 4 steps*

#### The spot price

The spot price of gold is the current market price per ounce for physical gold as a raw material, sometimes called spot gold. Gold ETFs that are backed by physical gold assets generally track the gold spot price.

The spot price is lower than what you'd pay to buy gold coins, bullion, or jewelry, since your total price will include a markup called the gold premium that covers refining, marketing, dealer overhead, and profits. The spot price is more like a wholesale price, and the spot price plus the gold premium is the retail price.

*Learn more: Thinking of buying gold? Here's what investors should watch for.*

#### Gold futures

Gold futures are contracts that mandate a gold transaction at a specific price on a future date. These contracts are exchange-traded and more liquid than physical gold. They settle on the contract expiration date or earlier, either financially or via delivery. A financial cash settlement involves paying the contract's profit or loss in cash. Delivery means the seller sends physical gold to the buyer for the contracted price.

#### Factors that affect gold prices

Supply and demand determine gold spot prices and gold futures prices. Factors that influence gold supply and demand include:

1. Geopolitical events
2. Central bank buying trends
3. Inflation
4. Interest rates
5. Mining production

title: Gold Prices Decline as US Dollar Strengthens and Investors Assess Geopolitical Risks
content_md:
Gold prices fell on Monday as the US dollar strengthened, while investors assessed developments surrounding a proposed energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, renewed attacks in the Middle East and the outlook for global inflation and interest rates.

At 05:01 ET (09:01 GMT), spot gold (XAU/USD) declined 0.5% to $4,174.23 per ounce, while gold futures fell 0.4% to $4,198.05.

Other precious metals also traded lower. Spot silver (XAG/USD) dropped 0.5% to $60.5075 per ounce, platinum (XPT/USD) declined 0.3% to $1,684.41, and palladium (XPD/USD) slipped 0.2% to $1,150.30. Palladium futures edged higher to $1,150.75.

The US dollar index advanced 0.1% to 102.31, adding pressure to dollar-denominated commodities. Gold had gained 1.3% during the previous week.

#### Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire Announcement and Middle East Tensions

US President Donald Trump announced that an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine had taken immediate effect, raising expectations of a possible reduction in disruptions to global fuel supplies.

Trump had previously called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries and said Moscow had agreed to release additional diesel supplies into international markets.

However, the ceasefire announcement had not been independently confirmed by both Russia and Ukraine, leaving uncertainty over whether attacks on energy infrastructure would stop.

Meanwhile, renewed violence in the Middle East continued to raise concerns about regional energy security.

King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, was reportedly targeted by Houthi forces on Sunday, following an attack on Saturday that killed 12 people and injured more than 300.

The Saturday incident was reported as the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia since the conflict involving Iran began in late February.

The Houthis described their operations as retaliation for what they characterised as Saudi aggression, including an attack on the airport in Yemen's capital, Sanaa.

The incidents have increased concerns about the potential for further regional disruption, particularly if attacks affect energy production, transportation or export infrastructure.

Although crude oil prices have recently eased, gold has declined by approximately 20% since the beginning of the US-Iran conflict in late February.

Higher energy costs can contribute to broader inflation pressures, potentially influencing central bank interest-rate decisions.

Rising interest rates can reduce the relative appeal of gold because the metal does not generate interest income, while bonds and other interest-bearing assets may offer higher yields.

title: Oil Prices Recover as Saudi Arabia Attacks Offset Expectations of Increased Russian Diesel Supplies
content_md:
Oil prices recovered from earlier losses on Monday as investors assessed the impact of attacks in Saudi Arabia and the Strait of Hormuz alongside US President Donald Trump's announcement of additional Russian diesel supplies.

Brent crude futures for December delivery increased by 69 cents, or 0.7%, to $105.41 per barrel by 09:23 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 57 cents, or 0.6%, to $92.42 per barrel.

The gains followed renewed concerns about energy supplies from the Middle East, where attacks on transport infrastructure and commercial shipping have continued.

The Iran-aligned Houthi movement claimed responsibility for an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday that reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300. Additional attacks were reported on Sunday.

Security concerns also increased around the Strait of Hormuz, where further incidents involving oil tankers have been reported this month.

United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said a tanker was struck by a drone near Sohar, Oman, while another vessel sustained damage while travelling through the strait.

The incidents raised questions about the recovery in Middle Eastern crude exports recorded during September, as continued attacks could disrupt shipping operations.

Goldman Sachs revised its December Brent crude forecast to $90 per barrel from $85, incorporating an estimated geopolitical risk premium of slightly more than $20 per barrel.

The bank also provided forecasts for US crude prices, citing the unusually wide difference between WTI and Brent.

"We forecast WTI prices, which are unusually low vs Brent because of high US-Europe shipping costs, to average $81 in December 2026 and $73 in 2027," Goldman Sachs analysts said.

Separately, Shell, Chevron and BP were preparing to return personnel to offshore facilities and resume production in the Gulf of Mexico following Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall early on Saturday.

#### Russian Diesel Announcement Weighs on Gasoil Futures

European gasoil futures declined 4.3% to $1,419.50 per metric tonne after Trump announced on Friday that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel to US and international markets.

The proposed shipments represent approximately 2.25 million barrels, with the president indicating that additional volumes could become available later.

However, analysts questioned Russia's capacity to increase exports following repeated attacks on its refining infrastructure.

"The immediate impact of the deal is questionable, as Russia's refining capacity has been severely reduced," PVM analyst Tamas Varga said.

title: Oil Prices Decline as Investors Await US Inflation Data and Bank Earnings Amid Geopolitical Tensions: Dow Jones, S&P, Nasdaq, Wall Street Futures
content_md:
Oil prices fell on Monday following US President Donald Trump's announcement of a proposed energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, although neither country had confirmed an agreement. Investors also turned their attention to upcoming US inflation figures, the start of the third-quarter corporate earnings season and continuing tensions in the Middle East.

Brent crude futures for December delivery declined 1.8% to $102.84 per barrel, reversing part of the nearly 3% increase recorded during the previous week.

Trump announced what he described as an immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, raising the possibility of reduced disruptions to Russian fuel supplies. However, military activity continued over the weekend, with reported Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure and further Russian strikes against Ukraine's electricity network.

The US president also called for Ukraine to halt attacks on Russian refineries and proposed increasing Russian diesel exports to the United States and international markets.

The feasibility of additional Russian fuel shipments remains uncertain, given the reported damage to domestic refining facilities and the need to maintain supplies within Russia.

A similar ceasefire initiative announced by Washington in September did not result in a confirmed agreement between Moscow and Kyiv.

#### US Inflation Report in Focus

Investors are preparing for Wednesday's US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, which could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's next interest-rate decision.

Forecasts cited in the report indicate that annual headline inflation could accelerate to 3.7%, while core inflation, which excludes food and energy, is expected to ease to 2.5%.

Market pricing currently suggests an approximately 18% probability of an interest-rate increase this month, reflecting reduced expectations of further monetary tightening.

The inflation figures will be assessed for indications of whether higher energy costs are affecting broader consumer prices.

A stronger-than-expected inflation reading could alter expectations for future Federal Reserve policy, while a moderation in underlying inflation would provide further evidence of easing price pressures.

#### US Bank Earnings Season Begins

Major US banks are scheduled to begin reporting third-quarter results on Tuesday, marking the start of a reporting period in which approximately 70% of S&P 500 companies are expected to publish earnings during October.

Analysts anticipate average earnings-per-share growth of approximately 30%, with businesses benefiting from artificial intelligence infrastructure investment accounting for more than half of the projected increase.

title: PM calls on Luxembourg to boost long-term investment and support international financial center
content_md:
Prime Minister Le Minh Hung has called on Luxembourg to encourage investment funds, financial institutions and businesses to increase long-term capital allocations to Vietnam, prioritising strategic infrastructure, renewable energy, technology, logistics, green finance and the development of Vietnam’s International Financial Centre.

The PM made the proposal during a meeting with Luxembourg Finance Minister Gilles Roth in Hanoi on October 12, during Mr. Roth’s visit to Vietnam.

To deepen bilateral cooperation, PM Hung urged both sides to implement the 2023 Strategic Partnership on Green Finance, the recently signed memorandum of understanding between their finance ministries, and the 2020 financial and banking cooperation protocol.

He called for these agreements to be translated into concrete action plans focusing on sustainable finance, capital markets, fund management, financial technology, workforce training, and stronger regulatory and supervisory capacity in the financial and banking sectors.

PM Hung also encouraged Luxembourg to help channel more capital from Luxembourg and Europe into Vietnam, particularly for essential infrastructure, renewable energy, logistics, fintech, digital assets, innovation, the green economy and green urban development.

He called on Luxembourg to support the development of green financial instruments and mobilize funding for Vietnam’s green transition through the Luxembourg House of Financial Technology.

Another priority is the development of Vietnam’s International Financial Centre, according to the PM. Luxembourg could share expertise in institutional development, asset and fund management, green finance and financial supervision, while helping train local professionals and connect Luxembourg-based financial institutions with Vietnam’s financial centre ecosystem from its early stages of operation.

The Government leader also urged Luxembourg to promote business connections and investment, encourage other EU member states to complete ratification of the EU–Vietnam Investment Protection Agreement (EVIPA), and help advance the Vietnam–EU Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

Minister Roth pledged to continue promoting cooperation, particularly in securities, bond issuance, transport infrastructure, digital finance and blockchain technology, supported by specific action plans.

As of September 2026, Luxembourg had 68 active FDI projects in Vietnam, with registered capital of approximately $2.79 billion. It ranked 19th among 154 countries and territories investing in Vietnam and fourth among EU member states.

title: F88 khai trương cửa hàng thứ 1.000
description: F88 đưa vào hoạt động cửa hàng thứ 1.000 tại Hà Nội, đồng thời đặt mục tiêu mở rộng mạng lưới lên 1.500-2.000 điểm vào năm 2030.
content_md:
F88 đưa vào hoạt động cửa hàng thứ 1.000 tại Hà Nội, đồng thời đặt mục tiêu mở rộng mạng lưới lên 1.500-2.000 điểm vào năm 2030.

Cửa hàng thứ 1.000 của F88 đặt tại khu vực ngã ba Chợ Hòa Lạc, Hà Nội chính thức đi vào hoạt động ngày 10/10. Từ những điểm giao dịch đầu tiên năm 2013, doanh nghiệp đã phát triển mạng lưới lên 1.000 cửa hàng trên toàn quốc sau hơn một thập kỷ hoạt động. Với quy mô hiện tại, F88 thuộc nhóm doanh nghiệp có mạng lưới cửa hàng lớn trong lĩnh vực cung cấp dịch vụ ngân hàng và tài chính tại Việt Nam.

Ông Phạm Trần Long, Phó tổng giám đốc F88, cho biết việc đạt mốc 1.000 cửa hàng đánh dấu bước phát triển về quy mô, đồng thời đặt ra yêu cầu cao hơn đối với công tác quản trị và vận hành hệ thống.

"Trong giai đoạn tiếp theo, chúng tôi sẽ tiếp tục mở rộng mạng lưới tại những khu vực có nhu cầu phù hợp, song song với nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động tại từng cửa hàng và chất lượng phục vụ khách hàng", ông Long nói.

Bên cạnh mở rộng mạng lưới trực tiếp, F88 phát triển nền tảng số MyF88 và hợp tác với các đối tác trong lĩnh vực thanh toán, ngân hàng, bảo hiểm. Việc kết hợp cửa hàng vật lý với kênh số giúp doanh nghiệp đa dạng hóa phương thức cung cấp dịch vụ, tiếp cận khách hàng tại nhiều khu vực.

Theo kế hoạch, F88 dự kiến nâng tổng số cửa hàng lên 1.050 trong năm 2026 và hướng tới 1.500-2.000 cửa hàng vào năm 2030. Song song với việc gia tăng độ phủ, doanh nghiệp tập trung phát triển công nghệ, cải thiện hiệu quả vận hành và quản lý chất lượng dịch vụ trên toàn hệ thống.

Đại diện F88 cho biết, trong giai đoạn tới, doanh nghiệp sẽ cân đối giữa tốc độ mở rộng mạng lưới và hiệu quả kinh doanh tại từng điểm giao dịch, nhằm duy trì chất lượng hoạt động khi quy mô hệ thống tiếp tục tăng.

title: Goldman Strategists Upgrade Global Stocks on Earnings Boost
content_md:
(Bloomberg) -- Goldman Sachs Group Inc. strategists are turning positive on global stocks for the short term, citing a boost from strong earnings for markets already trading near all-time highs.

Most Read from Bloomberg

- Ford Killed Its Electric Truck. Then Demand Surged
- Saudi Arabia Says 12 Dead, 309 Hurt in Riyadh Airport Attack
- Trump Says Russia and Ukraine Agreed to 'Energy Ceasefire'
- Deadly Attacks on Saudi Arabia Risk Wider War That Draws In US
- Bessent Will Likely Cut US Long Bond Sales Next Month, Says Citi

Equity prices are less demanding after higher oil prices and bond yields stalled the rally, while the outlook for profits is still healthy, the team led by Christian Mueller-Glissmann wrote in a note. They raised their three-month view on stocks to overweight from neutral, matching their bullish stance over a 12-month timeline.

"Earnings growth remains supportive for equities and the recent valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into the third-quarter earnings season," Mueller-Glissmann said.

The equity market is set for a high-stakes reporting season that will be crucial to sustaining the rally through to year-end. Analysts expect S&P 500 companies to post a 25% jump in third-quarter profits compared with a year earlier, among the best rates of increase on record, according to data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence.

The Goldman strategists expect stocks to surpass even that high bar.

Other Wall Street strategists, including at Bank of America Corp. and Barclays Plc, have also turned more bullish about the outlook for US stocks recently, citing among other things a robust earnings outlook.

The Goldman team prefers a "barbell strategy" of global tech names with selective rate-sensitive, bond-proxy stocks that have derated since the summer. They remain overweight on Asia and the US, and underweight on Europe.

They still view higher rates and energy prices as the main near-term risk to stocks, while the US midterm elections could also boost volatility.

The strategists remain neutral on bonds over three months, but have switched to overweight over 12 months. Allocations to bonds are becoming more attractive to those with longer investment horizons, they said.

"We believe bonds should gradually move from portfolio headwind to hedge," they noted.

title: US Dollar Price Forecast: DXY Eyes 102.49, Can EUR/USD Hold 1.1180 Ahead of CPI?
content_md:
#### **Dollar Index: Inflation Test Keeps Fed Policy in Focus**

The dollar remains supported by elevated U.S. borrowing costs and geopolitical tensions, while the focus is on the U.S. inflation report for next direction. Traders currently give a 81% probability of the Fed not changing policy rates at their October meeting, after weaker jobs data lessened the case for an immediate policy hike. Further increases in December or early 2027 remain a possibility if inflation doesn't decline.

Inflation forecasts are for U.S. headline inflation to hit 3.7% and core to be around 2.5% this month. Inflation data this week will be key for the dollar's outlook.

#### **EUR: French Debt Risk Counters ECB Tightening Expectations**

These forecasts were made by market participants or market analysts and reported by the source. Forecasts are not guaranteed to actually occur. Forecasts are not a reliable indicator of future performance.

France's fiscal situation still casts a shadow on the euro. The spread on 10-year bonds between France and Germany has risen to about 137 basis points and is approaching the levels last seen in 2012. This highlights the uncertainty in the market regarding France's ability to bring more budgetary discipline in the run up to the 2027 presidential elections.

Some help on monetary policy is expected. A Reuters poll showed that nearly 90% of economists expect the ECB to raise its 2.50% deposit rate by 25 basis points in December following a surge in euro-area inflation.

#### **GBP: Rate-Hike Expectations Meet a Difficult Budget Test**

Monetary policy is expected to be tightened in the UK as well with an above 80% chance of a Bank of England rate hike in November.

Fiscal policy is expected to be implemented to help ease the UK's cost-of-living concerns. The IFS estimates the government will need to find about £36 billion through tax rises or welfare cuts in the upcoming Budget on the 28th of October due to higher inflation, pressure on public services and increased defence spending.

#### **U.S. Dollar Index Technical Analysis: DXY Holds Above 102.10 as 102.49 Remains the Key Breakout Level**

Currently, the U.S. Dollar Index is trading around 102.24 on the 2-hour chart, and what catches my eye is how price is holding above the rising trendline and both moving averages. The large picture trend remains up, although price repeatedly failing around 102.49 shows that price still needs a clear breakout to push to higher levels.

102.49 is the first major level of resistance, and a break above that would likely bring 102.70, and 102.95 into the picture. Again, 102.10 is a key support, and if price continues to drop, 101.75 and 101.43 would come into play.

title: Asian stocks drift lower as AI anxiety hits South Korea; won at two-year high
content_md:
(Oct 12): South Korean shares dragged emerging Asian stock markets lower on Monday as investors grew wary of hefty AI-related spending and weak returns ahead of the earnings season, while broad US dollar selling lifted the won to a two-year high.

MSCI's broad index of emerging Asia stocks fell 0.8% to its lowest since mid-September. Tech-heavy South Korea and Taiwan markets account for more than half of the benchmark.

South Korea's Kospi closed down 3.7% after reopening from a long weekend, hitting its lowest since mid-August. Chip heavyweights Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix slipped 4.4% and 4.5%, respectively, hitting multi-week lows.

In Taiwan, the benchmark declined as much as 1.1% before recovering to end flat as trade resumed after a holiday. TSMC fell 1.6% in its steepest daily loss since mid-September, ahead of earnings later this week that are expected to show record quarterly profit.

Investor scrutiny has intensified over massive fundraising by technology firms to finance high-end AI chips, as high energy costs, expectations of further monetary tightening and rising sovereign debt drive borrowing costs higher.

South Korea accounted for the bulk of equity outflows from Asia excluding China last month, with foreigners selling US$17 billion (RM69.4 billion) worth of equities.

The Kospi has seen five straight months of foreign outflows, likely reflecting persistent concerns about valuations and the sustainability of the semiconductor supercycle, ANZ head of Asia research Khoon Goh said in a note.

In Indonesia, stocks dropped as much as 2% to hit their lowest since July. The Jakarta Composite Index benefited from bargain-hunting last week, gaining nearly 1% despite lingering concerns over market transparency and investability.

"Foreign investors sold roughly 2.45 trillion rupiah of equities last week, despite the index gaining," said Glenn Yin, director of research at ACCM.

"High US yields and expensive oil leave the market vulnerable: they challenge capital inflows, pressure the rupiah and limit room for monetary easing. Today’s decline appears consistent with that vulnerability."

Among currencies, the South Korean won appreciated to 1,332.16 per US dollar, its highest since October 2024. It has been among the region's best-performing currencies this year, rising nearly 8%.

Christopher Wong, FX strategist at OCBC, called the won's move "largely flow-driven", attributing it to exporter dollar sales despite foreign equity outflows alongside easing in long-term Treasury yields and softer oil prices.

"We see room for further KRW appreciation, particularly if USDKRW breaks decisively below the 1,320–1,330 support zone... Further easing in US yields and oil prices could reinforce this move, although KRW's high-beta characteristics also leave it vulnerable to a reversal in global risk sentiment," Wong said.

Meanwhile, the Indian rupee surged about 1% after the central bank diverted oil firms' dollar purchases from the spot market and moved to restrain corporate demand for forward dollars.

Other regional peers held their ground, with the MSCI EM currencies gauge up 0.3%, hitting its highest since mid-September.

title: BOK chief says early rate hike ahead of Fed's minimized economic costs
content_md:
**Lee Hyo-jin**

Bank of Korea (BOK) Gov. Shin Hyun-song said Monday that the central bank's August rate hike ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's September move gave Korea more time to respond and helped minimize the economic costs of monetary tightening.

"We signaled a shift toward higher interest rates earlier than many other major economies. By raising rates in August, ahead of the Fed's September hike, we bought ourselves time," Shin said during a parliamentary audit of the central bank.

"Taking action early carries far lower economic costs than having to raise rates defensively in response to market pressure," he added.

Shin said the preemptive move also helped guide market expectations, noting that the prospect of BOK's rate increases was reflected in bond yields and other market prices before the hikes actually took effect.

The BOK raised its policy rate by 0.25 percentage point in both July and August, bringing it to 3 percent. The Fed raised its benchmark rate by 0.25 percentage point in September, its first increase since July 2023, to a range of 3.75 percent to 4 percent.

During the audit, Shin left the door open to further rate hikes, warning that inflation is expected to remain above the BOK's 2 percent target for an extended period as cost pressures continue to pass through to consumer prices.

"One point we particularly take into account is that inflation hurts low income and vulnerable groups the most," Shin said in response to a question from Rep. Yoon Hu-duk of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea about possible rate hikes at the BOK's October and November policy meetings.

"The timing and pace of any further rate increases will depend on inflation and economic growth trends, as well as financial stability conditions," he said.

The governor also acknowledged that monetary tightening places a heavier burden on vulnerable households, as borrowers from lower income groups are hit harder by rate hikes.

The audit also saw opposition lawmakers question whether the government's expansionary fiscal policy would undermine the BOK's efforts to curb inflation through monetary tightening.

"Expansionary fiscal policy puts pressure on prices and the money supply in the short term," said Rep. Lee Jong-wook of the main opposition People Power Party.

Higher interest rates are intended to cool the economy by making borrowing more expensive and discouraging spending and investment. An expansionary fiscal policy, however, can have the opposite effect by injecting money into the economy and supporting demand.

In response, Shin said the BOK was using economic models to assess whether the two policies would work against each other.

He estimated that the government's budget proposal for next year would boost Korea's economic growth by 0.5 percentage point while adding 0.06 percentage point to inflation.

"If potential growth rises over the medium to long term, the two policies may not necessarily work against each other," Shin said.

title: BOK chief to attend G20, IMF-WBG meetings in Bangkok
content_md:
**Yonhap**

Korea's top central banker will attend a meeting of the Group of 20 (G20) finance ministers and central bank chiefs to be held in Thailand this week, the Bank of Korea (BOK) said Monday.

BOK Gov. Shin Hyun-song will join the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting, set to take place in Bangkok, where participants will discuss global economic conditions, growth and global imbalances, according to the central bank.

He will also attend the International Monetary Fund-World Bank Group (IMF-WBG) meetings, where discussions will focus on the global economic outlook and financial stability.

While in Bangkok, the BOK governor is scheduled to hold separate talks with high-ranking officials from the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank and other major central banks to exchange views on recent international developments.

He will also participate in CNN's Global Perspectives, a live event series convening leaders, CEOs and innovators for conversations on issues covering culture, technology and business, along with Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria, director-general of the World Trade Organization, and Bernard Mensah, president of International at Bank of America, according to the BOK.

title: Ngôi nhà đưa góc trưng bày xe cổ vào phòng khách
description: Để thỏa đam mê sưu tầm xe cổ của chủ nhà, kiến trúc sư thiết kế đường dẫn đưa ôtô vào thẳng phòng khách, làm điểm nhấn cho toàn bộ không gian sống.
content_md:
Để thỏa đam mê sưu tầm xe cổ của chủ nhà, kiến trúc sư thiết kế đường dẫn đưa ôtô vào thẳng phòng khách, làm điểm nhấn cho toàn bộ không gian sống.

Ngôi nhà một tầng tại quận Thuận Nghĩa, cách trung tâm Bắc Kinh (Trung Quốc) khoảng 35 km về phía đông bắc.

Trước cải tạo, ngôi nhà có diện tích 110 m2. Nhóm kiến trúc sư giữ lại công trình cũ, kết hợp xây thêm các không gian chức năng, nâng tổng diện tích ở lên gần gấp ba (290 m2). Một khu vườn rộng 180 m2 được bố trí bên ngoài tòa nhà, là góc nghỉ ngơi, thư giãn cùng không gian xanh của gia đình 4 người.

Để thích ứng với mùa đông lạnh tại Bắc Kinh, công trình sử dụng hệ thống bao che cách nhiệt liên tục, kết hợp cửa ra vào và cửa sổ có khả năng giữ nhiệt.

Chủ nhà có sở thích sưu tầm ôtô cổ, môtô và xe đạp, nên mong muốn có không gian đủ rộng để đưa chiếc Toyota Land Cruiser cổ và môtô Harley-Davidson vào phòng khách.

Từ yêu cầu này, kiến trúc sư đưa ra giải pháp kết hợp không gian trưng bày xe với khu vực sinh hoạt chung, thay vì bố trí gara theo cách thông thường.

Phòng khách được tổ chức quanh lò sưởi trung tâm và hệ sofa cong kích thước lớn, tạo khu vực quây quần cho gia đình, tiếp đón bạn bè.

Phía sau khu vực tiếp khách, kiến trúc sư bố trí lối đi uốn cong, đủ để ôtô và môtô di chuyển vào bên trong. Đây cũng là không gian trưng bày bộ sưu tập xe của gia chủ. Bề mặt lối đi được lát đá cuội thô, tạo sự khác biệt với sàn bê tông mài tại sảnh sinh hoạt.

Dọc theo lối đi dành cho xe, nhóm thiết kế bố trí bức tường cong, sử dụng vật liệu hoàn thiện tương tự mặt ngoài công trình. Chi tiết này tạo sự liên tục giữa kiến trúc ngoại và nội thất.

Một ô cửa tròn trên tường dẫn vào phòng học và sáng tạo dành cho 2 trẻ nhỏ. Không gian được bố trí bàn ghế đơn giản, có thể di chuyển và thay đổi vị trí theo nhu cầu học tập, vui chơi. Phía trên phòng học có giếng trời, giúp bổ sung ánh sáng tự nhiên.

Ở đầu còn lại của bức tường cong, kiến trúc sư bố trí khu bếp mở, liên thông với phòng ăn và phòng khách. Từ vị trí nấu nướng, chủ nhà có thể quan sát phần lớn không gian sinh hoạt chung, thuận tiện theo dõi hoạt động của các thành viên.

Phòng ăn sử dụng bàn trắng có bánh xe, kết hợp các mẫu ghế khác nhau về kiểu dáng và màu sắc.

Nhóm thiết kế ưu tiên chiều cao trần và khả năng tiếp cận ánh sáng tự nhiên. Toàn bộ không gian sinh hoạt chung có chiều cao lên tới 3,5 m.

Giải pháp hoàn thiện đơn giản giúp làm nổi bật cấu trúc đường cong, đồng thời tạo sự thống nhất giữa các khu vực chức năng.

Khu vực ngoài trời được bố trí bàn ghế trên thảm cỏ. Từ sân vườn có thể quan sát không gian tiếp khách và khu vực trưng bày ôtô cổ phía sau.

Khu vệ sinh sử dụng gạch ốp tường màu xanh nhạt, kết hợp hệ tủ lavabo treo tường và hai bồn rửa đặt bàn. Vách kính lớn sát trần mở tầm nhìn ra bể bơi ngoài trời, giúp không gian đón ánh sáng tự nhiên.

Mặt bằng công trình được tổ chức trên một tầng, với lối đi uốn cong dành cho ôtô và môtô chạy qua khu sinh hoạt chung.

**Bích Phương** (theo *Gooood*)
